# logflare_alert (Resource)

Logflare alert. Setting `rule_key` makes it an alert issue rule: each run turns result rows into alert issues.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An alert issue rule: one alert issue per Edge Function returning 5xx responses.
resource "logflare_alert" "edge_function_5xx" {
  name        = "Edge Function errors"
  description = "An Edge Function returned 5xx responses in the last hour."
  language    = "pg_sql"
  query       = <<-SQL
    select body -> 'metadata' ->> 'function_id' as function_id, count(*) as errors
    from function_edge_logs
    where timestamp > now() - interval '1 hour'
      and (body -> 'metadata' ->> 'status_code')::int >= 500
    group by 1
  SQL
  cron        = "*/5 * * * *"
  rule_key    = "supabase.edge-function-5xx"
  managed     = true
  severity    = "major"
  category    = "health"
  group_by    = ["function_id"]
  scope       = { project = "default" }

  signal_mapping = {
    preview = { lql = "f:function_edge_logs m.function_id:{{function_id}} m.status_code:>=500" }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `cron` (String) Cron schedule
- `language` (String) Query language: `bq_sql`, `pg_sql` or `lql`
- `name` (String) Name of the alert
- `query` (String) Query run on every schedule tick

### Optional

- `category` (String) Alert issue category: `security`, `performance` or `health`
- `description` (String) Description of the alert
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the alert runs
- `group_by` (List of String) Result columns that split rows into separate alert issues
- `managed` (Boolean) Whether the rule is a managed preset
- `resolve_after_runs` (Number) Clean runs before an alert issue resolves
- `rule_key` (String) Stable key of the alert issue rule, e.g. `supabase.edge-function-5xx`. Makes this alert an alert issue rule.
- `scope` (Map of String) Literal identifiers added to every alert issue, e.g. `{ project = "default" }`
- `severity` (String) Alert issue severity: `critical`, `major`, `warning` or `info`
- `signal_mapping` (Attributes) How result rows become alert issue signals (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--signal_mapping))

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Alert identifier
- `token` (String) Alert token used by the Logflare API

<a id="nestedatt--signal_mapping"></a>
### Nested Schema for `signal_mapping`

Optional:

- `category_column` (String) Column that overrides the category
- `description_column` (String) Column used as the alert issue description
- `identifiers` (Map of String) Identifier key to result column
- `metadata_columns` (List of String) Columns copied into the alert issue metadata
- `notebook` (Attributes List) SQL templates shown as notebook cells on each alert issue (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--signal_mapping--notebook))
- `preview` (Attributes) Log preview shown on each alert issue (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--signal_mapping--preview))
- `severity_column` (String) Column that overrides the severity
- `title_column` (String) Column used as the alert issue title
- `window_seconds` (Number) Look-back window for `lql` rules

<a id="nestedatt--signal_mapping--notebook"></a>
### Nested Schema for `signal_mapping.notebook`

Required:

- `source` (String) `database` or `logs`
- `sql` (String) SQL with `{{ident:key}}` and `{{literal:key}}` placeholders
- `title` (String) Cell title


<a id="nestedatt--signal_mapping--preview"></a>
### Nested Schema for `signal_mapping.preview`

Optional:

- `lql` (String) LQL with `f:<source>` and `{{identifier}}` placeholders

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by alert id or alert token.
terraform import logflare_alert.example 123
```
